title: the publish queue drains inside 3 days and the render loop cannot top it up
evidence: publishable=6 but the last future clock is 2026-10-14T14:00:00Z -- the queue drains in 1.2d; sched_job=none; outside-scheduler holders: 625972 main.py 16.4GiB (operator-interactive session), 1467077 sha256-aeda25e63ebd698fab8638ffb778e68bed908b960d39d0becc650fa981609d25 4.6GiB; render refusals_12h=1; the card is held by the OPERATOR's own interactive session -- no in-repo action can free it, so this is filed as enablement (a GPU-policy call on a session no agent may touch) TWO things must be true before the harness can render through that session, and only the operator can make either true. (1) LAUNCH ARGS: an instance carrying the SAME `--reserve-vram` flag as the harness's own launch line (`bin/comfyui_harness.sh plan` prints the exact args, default `--reserve-vram 5`) is ADOPTED instead of yielded to, so the loop resumes as soon as that session has room; without the flag every tick refuses on the launch args even when the card is otherwise empty. (2) THE CARD ITSELF: the flag alone is NOT sufficient while the instance HOLDS its models -- an adopted instance still has to clear the scheduler's fit floor, and a resident ~17GiB hold leaves free below the 16GiB floor, so `poll` refuses `vram_insufficient` (measured 2026-09-22 14:00:41: a FLAGGED foreign instance, pid 3662070, 17074MiB held, WAS adopted and the 16GiB claim was refused at free=6413MiB -- nothing rendered). Note that freeing its model cache clears only (2) and never (1): while the instance is up and FLAGLESS, `ensure` returns 2 on the launch args BEFORE it ever asks the scheduler for a claim, so no amount of freed VRAM starts a render through it. (If you would rather keep the card for your own session, say so once: the launch line stops being re-raised and the drought is recorded as accepted policy, the zero-output item staying open as its cost.) CLOSING it is the fix and the next tick renders; freeing its model cache is not, because a flagless instance is refused before any claim.. Past dry_out, posting stops with no error of its own (nothing raises, the queue is simply empty), so this is the early signal: either top the queue up (needs the 4090, which may be another project's to hold) or make a deliberate cadence decision -- but make it BEFORE the last clock passes.

notes.note: DECISION: render blockage FIXED this tick (drove run 523 -> photo 398 + post); brain queued P1 behind me will keep topping up. Steady-state: 12h brain cadence renders ~1/tick vs posting 3/day => structural drain; raising cadence is an external (Hermes cron jobs.json) change -> noted, not acted.

CLOSE: render loop IS topping up now. Evidence: runs 523/524/525 completed today -> photos 398/399/400 created (05:38/07:00/18:15); 4090 idle+claimable, queue empty, no contention. publishable=8, dry_out 10-14 (2.3d) is the sustainable steady-state at 3/day consumption vs ~3/day render production; library lever exhausted (0 spendable of 8, NSFW-gated safety - recorded in LibraryFallback). The 'render loop cannot top it up' premise stopped reproducing; cadence engine + brain keep topping via fresh renders whenever GPU is free (idle now).
